html:
Delhi is a city on the Yamuna river in north India and the seat of many of the subcontinent's empires. Today it is a huge metropolis that contains New Delhi, the capital of India.

It has been rebuilt again and again on nearby sites, so people speak of the "seven cities of Delhi". Rajput rulers held a fort here by the 1000s. After 1192 the Turkic conquerors from Afghanistan made it their base, and in 1206 it became the capital of the Delhi Sultanate. They raised the Qutb Minar beside the far older iron pillar, and later dynasties built new walled towns nearby. The poet Amir Khusrau lived here. Timur sacked the city in 1398.

Under the Mughals it gained Humayun's Tomb, and from 1639 Shah Jahan built Shahjahanabad, today's Old Delhi, with the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid. The Persian ruler Nader Shah sacked it in 1739 and carried off the Peacock Throne.

The British took Delhi in 1803. It was a centre of the great rebellion of 1857, after which the last Mughal emperor was exiled; the poet Ghalib lived through that year. In 1911 the British moved their capital here from Calcutta and built New Delhi. At the Partition of 1947 many Muslims left and hundreds of thousands of refugees from Punjab arrived.
sum: Delhi is a city on the Yamuna river in north India and the seat of many of the subcontinent's empires. Today it is a huge metropolis that contains New Delhi, the capital of India.
